plan.question: Our Muon optimizer currently uses a fixed airbench quintic (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) for Newton-Schulz, probably with about 3 iterations, on conv filters. If we switch to per-iteration minimax-optimal coefficients (Polar Express or similar) and keep the same iteration count, does that improve accuracy per step for a small CNN trained for about 9 epochs at batch 2048 in bf16? What decides the effect? Specifically: how the orthogonalization error (the singular-value spread after k iterations) depends on the coefficient schedule and the iteration count; whether a more exact polar factor helps or hurts optimization compared with the deliberately loose airbench/Keller quintic, which only maps singular values into roughly [0.7, 1.2]; whether bf16 stability needs safety margins or renormalization; and whether reported gains appear at very short horizons or low iteration counts, or only in LLM pretraining.
queries: Polar Express optimal polynomial Newton-Schulz Muon
minimax polynomial polar decomposition bfloat16 iterations
Muon optimizer approximate orthogonalization error convergence
Muon CNN CIFAR speedrun Newton-Schulz iterations
rubric: Compares Newton-Schulz or polar-factor polynomial coefficient schedules (fixed quintic vs per-iteration/optimal) inside Muon or a similar orthogonalized-momentum optimizer, and reports a training-quality metric (loss or accuracy per step), not only matrix approximation error.
Reports the effect at a low iteration count (<= 5) or analyzes how approximation quality, such as the singular-value interval after k steps, maps onto optimization progress.
Covers low-precision (bf16) numerical stability of the iteration, e.g. safety factors, normalization, or divergence.
Preferably includes small-scale or vision/CNN experiments, or short-horizon training budgets, rather than only large LLM pretraining.
exclude: Methods requiring pretrained weights or external data
Test-time augmentation or any use of the test set
Approaches needing new package installs beyond PyTorch 2.4.0 / torchvision 0.19.0
Distributed/multi-GPU-only Muon systems work with no single-GPU relevance
Classical numerical-analysis polar decomposition papers with no connection to optimizers or training
